key_insight: Eu²⁺/Eu³⁺ redox chemistry pins the Fermi level, overcoming self-limiting nitrogen incorporation in titanate-derived perovskite oxynitrides.
engineering_relevance: Fermi-level control offers a strategy for tuning oxynitride composition during synthesis, though photovoltaic performance was not evaluated.
method: Combine theoretical defect modelling with experimental oxynitride characterisation.
Vary A-site composition in Eu–Ba and Eu–Ca titanate-derived oxynitrides.
Quantify nitrogen uptake using hot gas extraction.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports nitrogen contents up to 0.03 per formula unit in barium titanate-derived oxynitrides versus 0.65 in Eu-containing compositions, with Fermi-level pinning approximately 2.9 eV above the valence-band maximum.
watch_item: Further nitrogen incorporation remains limited by bond-angle distortion within Ti(O,N)₆ octahedra.
paper_title: Controlling nitrogen incorporation in (Eu,Ba,Ca)TiO$_3$-derived perovskite-type oxynitrides through Fermi Level Engineering
